demos.title: Notification bell
demos.description: The nav entry with its unread badge: the count from the feed's own page envelope, the accessible name carrying it, and nothing at all drawn at zero.

variants.description: Three waiting — the count is in the badge and in the button's accessible name.
A busy account: past 99 the badge reads 99+ rather than resizing the nav for a number nobody acts on.
Nothing unread: the bell alone, no badge. The same picture a failed read gets — the bell never invents a number it does not have.

demos.title: Notification feed list
demos.description: The feed as a self-contained skin: unread dot and count, mark-all, type glyph, title, one-line body, relative time in a <time> carrying the exact instant, and the whole row as a link when data carries a deep link.

variants.description: Two unread rows, both with somewhere to go: the dot on each, the count above, and mark-all live.
The socket will not come back on its own. The reason is stated and Reconnect is right there — never a silent fall back to polling.
Two unread over two already read, with more pages behind them. The difference between a read row and an unread one is the thing to look at here — it has to survive being scanned, not read.
Nothing left unread: no dots, no badge, and mark-all switched OFF with the sentence saying why beside it — never a live button whose only outcome is marked: 0.

demos.title: Notifications page
demos.description: The page the nav routes to: a heading, the delivery mode (live socket or the documented 60s poll), and the feed with a real row anatomy — type glyph, title, body, relative time, deep link.

variants.description: No realtime extra on this deployment: the newest page is refetched every 60s while the tab is visible, and the indicator says so.
A socket is carrying the feed — new rows arrive as frames.
The same page at desktop width: the list fills its container up to a reading measure instead of staying a 340px card.
Read, and there was nothing. The only state allowed to say so — and it says it alone, not as a footer under rows.

demos.title: Push notification settings
demos.description: The push settings surface: a switch whose position comes from GET /devices/ matched on this device's token fingerprint, and the account's registry with an inactive device flagged and removal by row id behind a confirm sheet.

variants.description: This device plus an old phone the push provider rejected — listed and flagged, because hiding it would draw the account as smaller than it is.
Nothing registered yet: a designed empty state with the door in it.
An insecure origin or a browser without push. The reason sits beside the control and the switch is off-limits, rather than a dead grey rectangle.
Three devices at desktop width, on a settings column measure.
The switch on its own, for a host that puts the registry elsewhere.
The registry on its own — every device the account sends to.
